models.collectorNote: Chrysler mechanicals make the engine the easy part; trim, brightwork and that dashboard are the restoration's real budget.

generations.name: HK500
generations.note: Early cars used the 5.9-litre Chrysler at 335 hp before the 6.3 arrived; the manual gearbox was a Pont-à-Mousson four-speed, most cars took Chrysler's TorqueFlite automatic.

models.intro: France's last great luxury GT at full strength: Jean Daninos's Facel Vega with a 6.3-litre Chrysler V8, a tubular chassis, and an interior finished like a Parisian salon, including the famous painted faux-wood dashboard, done by hand. Stirling Moss drove his across Europe between races.
models.name: HK500

models.collectorNote: Fewer than half are thought to survive; completeness of the interior fittings decides a car's fate more than its body.

generations.name: Excellence EX1 / EX2
generations.note: The EX2 of 1961 restyled the fins away and adopted the HK500/Facel II running gear.

models.intro: A pillarless four-door hardtop on the grand scale, suicide rear doors, a Chrysler V8, and a price that bought several Citroën DSs. About 230 were built for kings, ambassadors and Ava Gardner; it remains the only French post-war car built to true American-limousine scale.
models.name: Excellence

models.collectorNote: A rebuilt Marchisio engine by a known specialist transforms the ownership story; the Facel III is the pragmatic classic of the three.

generations.name: Facellia / Facel III / Facel 6
generations.note: The Facel III substituted Volvo's rugged 1.8-litre four (108 hp) and sold better than the original; about 1,900 Facellias were built against plan for many more.

models.intro: The little Facel, built to sell in volume with a twin-cam four designed by Carlo Marchisio, a jewel of an engine that proved fatally fragile in service and sank the company under warranty claims. Its successors (Facel III, with a Volvo engine, and the six-cylinder Facel 6) were the rescue attempt.
models.name: Facellia

models.collectorNote: The market treats the Facel II as France's blue-chip GT; documentation from the Amicale Facel Vega's archives is the provenance standard.

generations.name: Facel II
generations.note: The 6.7-litre cars with the manual gearbox are the quickest Facels; quoted figures vary between gross ratings by year.

models.intro: Daninos called it the finest Facel of all, and the styling backs him: the HK500's successor cleaned the lines, stacked the headlamps, and kept the Chrysler power and the hand-finished cabin. Only 184 were built before Facel closed in October 1964.
models.name: Facel II
